mbb_1981_82.verdict: CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY that Biola was the NAIA's No. 1 team in 1981-82: the UPI wire (March 1982) says Biola was No. 1 'throughout the season', and the NAIA's own championship guides (1988, 1997) list Biola as No. 1 in the FINAL 1982 coaches' poll and the tournament's No. 1 seed (35-0 entering). NOT independently verified: the specific 'eight straight weeks' / 'first NAIA team to hold No. 1 for eight straight weeks' claim and the individual weekly polls. No weekly 1981-82 NAIA poll table was found. For context, the NAIA ran nine regular-season ratings in 1987-88 ('9th and final rating'), so eight straight weeks at No. 1 fits 'throughout the season' but is still unconfirmed. Biola's own 1982 yearbook words it differently ('set a national record by maintaining consistent victory for eight successive weeks'), which suggests the claim may have changed as it was retold.

mbb_1981_82.caution: Cal Lutheran Echo 1983-02-11 calls Biola 'ranked second nationally last year'. That most likely refers to the national runner-up finish, not a poll, and it conflicts with the sources above. It is not used.

gaps: 1981-82 weekly NAIA polls: no poll table found. The Idaho Times-News (Nov 1981-Mar 1982, 80 issues searched) did not print NAIA polls. archive.org full-text search found no 1982 newspaper poll table naming Biola. Sports Illustrated 1982 scans on archive.org have almost no OCR text. The Google News Archive (Ellensburg Daily Record, Lewiston Tribune, Spokane Chronicle, Kentucky New Era, etc.) has page images only and was not searched page by page; this is the best remaining route.
The 1981-82 'eight straight weeks' claim is unverified. The best independent statements are UPI's 'No. 1 ... throughout the season' and the NAIA's 'No. 1 in final poll'.

NAIA tournament programs for 1978, 1980, 1981, 1983, 1984, 1985, 1990 and 1994-96 are on archive.org without OCR text (images only), so they were not searched. The 1983 program probably reprints the 1982 final poll.

Men's basketball 1964-1995 is sparse: only 1971-72 (district), 1974-75 (receiving votes), 1980-81 (14th), 1981-82, 1985-86 (5th) and 1987-88 (final 8th, previous 9th) were found. 1990s seasons other than 1995-96, 1996-97 and 1997-98 were not found.
Women's basketball: AIAW-era rankings (1977-78 4th; 1980-81 4th and 3rd) come from opponents' student papers. The AIAW division is inferred from the text ('Division II').
Women's volleyball: the 1997 NAIA runner-up season has only the ca. Sept. 25, 1997 No. 3 mention; no weekly or final 1997 poll was found. 1982's 'fourth-rated' does not name the association.
Women's soccer 2004 NAIA runner-up season: weekly ranks come only from the Biola EagleSports Weekly newsletter (biola-news). The NAIA final poll was not found.
No pre-2003 rankings were found for baseball, softball, cross country, track, tennis or swimming.

Excluded on purpose: EagleSports Weekly and old-site rows for men's/women's basketball 2003-05, volleyball 2003-04 and women's tennis 2004, because primary NAIA polls for those are already in basketball.json, volleyball.json and other-sports.json. Also excluded: the ambiguous 'National Rank - 28th' in the 11-29-04 and 12-6-04 basketball boxes (the two-column layout makes it unclear which team it belongs to), NAIA Directors' Cup items (directors-cup.json), tournament seeds, and individual rankings.
